subject.title: [voice-call] OpenAI realtime: audio clipping / breaking inside words during first ~30s of outbound calls (Twilio mulaw output)

question: Is the current report plus source path enough to choose an OpenAI-to-Twilio audio mitigation, or should maintainers require a fresh current-main call/audio artifact first?
rationale: The reported release already used the main suspected format and resampling pieces, so maintainer judgment is needed before changing shared realtime audio without live evidence.

options.title: Require live diagnosis first
options.body: Keep this open for a current-main Twilio/OpenAI call, redacted audio/logs, or level/queue instrumentation before changing shared realtime audio.

options.title: Land instrumentation only
options.body: Add narrowly scoped output-level and queue diagnostics first, then use the collected evidence to choose the audio fix.

options.title: Accept a mitigation now
options.body: Apply a small gain or pacing change based on the existing report, accepting the risk that the wrong layer may be changed.

recommendation.title: Require live diagnosis first
recommendation.body: Keep this open for a current-main Twilio/OpenAI call, redacted audio/logs, or level/queue instrumentation before changing shared realtime audio.

likelyOwner.reason: They are tied to the Voice Call realtime pacing path and release history most directly connected to the reported output leg.
